abstract: Traditional mass spectrometry-based glycoproteomic approaches have been widely used for site-specific N -glycoform analysis, but due to the complexity of heavily glycosylated glycoproteins, they require large amounts of starting material, often include a complicated workflow, and depend on very challenging data analysis. These limitations have prevented glycoproteomics from being adapted to a high-throughput platform, and the sensitivity of the analysis is currently inadequate for elucidating N -glycan heterogeneity in clinical samples. Heavily glycosylated spike proteins of enveloped viruses, recombinantly expressed as potential vaccines, are prime targets for such an analysis. Since the immunogenicity of spike proteins may be impacted by their glycosylation patterns, site-specific analysis of N -glycoforms provides critical information for vaccine design. DeGlyPHER is an ultrasensitive, simple, rapid, robust, and efficient approach for site-specific analysis of viral N -glycoforms that we developed for the analysis of limited quantities of viral glycoproteins, such as in patient samples. DeGlyPHER employs a “single-pot” modification to our previously reported sequential deglycosylation strategy.
